questions.question: Write any three types of IPR.
questions.solution_html:
• Write any three types of IPR. (3 Marks)
  • Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) are legal rights granted to the creator or owner of a
  • creation of the mind, such as an invention, literary or artistic work, design, or symbol. These
  • rights provide the owner with exclusive rights over the use of their creation for a certain
  • period.
  • Types of IPRs:
  • ● Patents – Protect inventions.
  • ● Trademarks – Protect brand names, logos, and symbols.
  • ● Copyrights – Protect creative works (books, music, films, software).
  • ● Geographical Indications (GIs) – Protect products linked to a specific location.
  • ● Industrial Designs – Protect appearance or shape of a product.
  • ● Trade Secrets – Protect confidential business information.
  • ● Plant Variety Rights – Protect new plant varieties.
  • *Award marks for any three valid types of IPR.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: *Award marks for any three valid types of IPR.

questions.question: What is a Private Limited Company?
questions.solution_html:
• What is a Private Limited Company? (5 Marks)
  • A Private Limited Company is a company registered under the Companies Act and owned by
  • private individuals. It has a separate legal entity from its owners, and the liability of its
  • members is limited to the amount unpaid on the shares held by them.
  • Key Features:
  • ● Minimum 2 members and maximum 200 members,Minimum 2 directors,Separate
  • legal entity,Limited liability of shareholders,Restriction on transfer of shares,Cannot
  • invite the public to subscribe to its shares.

questions.question: Compare the management style of family businesses with professionally managed companies using suitable Indian cases.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the management style of family businesses with professionally managed
  • companies using suitable Indian cases.
  • Difference Between Family Businesses and Professionally Managed Companies
  • Ownership and Control
  • Family Businesses: In family businesses, ownership and control remain with family members.
  • Examples include Murugappa Group, Dabur, Wadia Group, Godrej Group, and Kirloskar
  • Group.
  • Professionally Managed Companies: In professionally managed companies, ownership and
  • management are separate. Examples include Infosys, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Larsen &
  • Toubro.
  • Leadership
  • Family Businesses: Family businesses are usually led by members of the owning family.
  • Professionally Managed Companies: Professionally managed companies are led by qualified
  • professional managers.
  • Decision Making
  • Family Businesses: Family businesses often have centralized and quick decision-making.
  • Professionally Managed Companies: Professionally managed companies follow formal
  • procedures and collective decision-making.
  • Succession
  • Family Businesses: In family businesses, leadership is generally passed on to the next
  • generation of the family.
  • Professionally Managed Companies: In professionally managed companies, leadership
  • positions are filled based on merit and competence.
  • Recruitment
  • Family Businesses: Family businesses may prefer family members for key positions.
  • Professionally Managed Companies: Professionally managed companies recruit and promote
  • employees based on qualifications and performance.
  • Objectives
  • Family Businesses: Family businesses focus on preserving family legacy and ensuring long-
  • term continuity.
  • Professionally Managed Companies: Professionally managed companies focus on
  • profitability, growth, and maximizing shareholder wealth.
  • Management Style
  • Family Businesses: Family businesses tend to have a more informal management structure.
  • Professionally Managed Companies: Professionally managed companies have a formal and
  • systematic management structure.
  • Conclusion
  • Family businesses such as Murugappa Group, Dabur, Wadia Group, Godrej Group, and
  • Kirloskar Group are characterized by family ownership and succession. Professionally
  • managed companies such as Infosys, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Larsen & Toubro rely on
  • professional expertise and merit-based management.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: professional expertise and merit-based management.
